calibration_gold_only_miss.title: A tag already captured by a biomaterial characteristic is redundant
calibration_gold_only_miss.snippet: Tags fill gaps the FactorValues and biomaterial characteristics don't already cover. A tag that just restates a constant BM characteristic the loader already ingests is redundant — don't add it.

calibration_agent_extra.title: When an experiment tag is needed
calibration_agent_extra.snippet: Emit a tag only when the property holds for EVERY profiled sample and falls in a tag-worthy category. What a study is 'about' or 'relevant to' is never a tagging reason.

calibration_tag_match_near.title: Same concept, two bindings — choose one (a swap, not add+remove)
calibration_tag_match_near.snippet: When the agent and the baseline name the SAME concept with different labels or URIs, that's a single relabel/swap — keep one binding — not a disconnected add + remove.

D8c.title: Baseline markers belong only on the baseline FV
D8c.snippet: The five canonical baseline tokens (reference substance role, reference subject role, wild type genotype, initial time point, control) belong ONLY on the baseline FV. A non-baseline FV must not carry one — neither as a bare subject nor as '<X> + has role + <token>' on a treatment arm.

D8.title: Contrast factors need a baseline FV — reference-less factors (organism part, cell line) don't
D8.snippet: A categorical factor whose levels form a real contrast needs exactly one FV marked baseline (via is_baseline or a canonical baseline marker: reference substance/subject role, control, wild type genotype, or initial time point), because DEA computes each level against that baseline. Factors with no natural reference level — organism part, cell line, cell type — don't require one: there's no principled control among levels like lung vs heart. If no baseline is set Gemma just picks one (by a convention such as lexical order; the sex factor is hard-coded to female), so it's harmless for a curator or agent to mark a baseline even when it isn't needed. Such reference-less factors may instead be subset for DEA — an independent analysis run within each level rather than contrasting across them (e.g. one DEA for choroid plexus, another for prefrontal cortex). Don't subset when the across-level comparison is itself the point of the study; and when GEO has merged several distinct experiments into one record the fix is splitExperiment, not a baseline. Panel / batch / continuous / single-level factors are baseline-exempt for their own reasons.

links.title: Curating Experimental Factor Categories and Factor Values

calibration_factor_extra.title: Is this axis an experimental factor (EFC)?
calibration_factor_extra.snippet: A factor must be a real experimental contrast that varies across samples and is in the EFC catalog. Tumour vs adjacent-normal of the same organ is 'disease', not 'organism part' (which distinguishes anatomical sites).

calibration_factor_gold_only_miss.title: A varying, DEA-relevant axis should be a factor
calibration_factor_gold_only_miss.snippet: If an axis varies across samples and matters for the analysis, it should be an EFC. Block / batch / assay / platform are populated by the loader, not proposed by the agent.
